description: Uniform landmark cost partitioning turns landmarks into an admissible heuristic: it never overestimates the cost to the goal. A *landmark* is a fact that is true at some point of every plan. Each operator shares its cost equally among the landmarks it can achieve that are still false; each landmark is worth its cheapest share; the estimate is the sum. Every plan must achieve each landmark, and no operator pays more than its cost in total, so A* with this heuristic finds optimal plans. It is cheap to compute, but often weaker than the optimal partitioning.

papers.title: Cost-Optimal Planning with Landmarks
papers.venue: International Joint Conference on Artificial Intelligence (IJCAI)
